title: Geometrically Significant Surfaces of Black Holes from a Single Scalar
summary: Black hole spacetimes contain several geometrically distinguished hypersurfaces, including event and Cauchy horizons, stationary-limit surfaces, and curvature singularities. These structures are usually identified by different geometric or causal criteria. We show that, for the Kerr--Newman black hole, the membrane-paradigm pressure of a stretched horizon admits an analytically continued scalar representative whose fully factorized form has zeros, poles, and singular factors aligned with these standard Kerr--Newman loci.
